title: Weighted protective slices and burn-rate circuit-breakers for model endpoints
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: We lack a single, operational SLI/SLO spec that treats latency, availability, and model-quality as first-class signals while allowing per-endpoint and per-variant weighting. When regional capacity is constrained we need automated, predictable behavior: (1) prioritized retention of SLAs for premium customers, (2) controlled degradation for best-effort routes, and (3) safety to avoid noisy regressions from model variants consuming disproportionate error budget.

Goal: Define and implement (a) a weighted error-budget accounting model that supports per-customer and per-route priorities via "protective slices", (b) burn-rate driven circuit-breaker thresholds that factor both latency and model-quality signal regressions, and (c) an automated soft-eviction load-shedding strategy plus multi-region warm-reserve failover choreography. This ticket scopes the SLI definitions, thresholds, orchestration triggers, and a runbook for operators and incident responders.
acceptance_criteria: SLI taxonomy document published in Confluence: includes latency, availability, token-cost-normalized quality SLI and per-variant weighting
Protective slice allocator implemented in controller that maps routes -> slices with percent of total error budget reserved
Circuit-breaker service prototype that consumes burn-rate, p99 latency, and model-quality alerts and emits action decisions (throttle, fallback, quiesce) to router
Soft-eviction algorithm implemented: reduces concurrency by route priority, preserves admission for premium slices, and logs decisions for audit
Multi-region failover play documented: warm-reserve allocation, passive capacity thresholds, and evacuation steps tested in staging with a canary workload
Grafana dashboards showing combined burn-rate, slice-level budgets, and historical enforcement events
Runbook with operator steps for manual override, budget transfers, and postmortem checklist
decisions: Adopt composite SLI = weighted combination of availability (5xx and timeouts), latency tail (p95/p99), and model-quality score (promptset-based embedding similarity / error-rate). Weights default to 50% latency, 30% availability, 20% quality for low-latency routes; configurable per-route.

Define protective slices as immutable short-term reservations (daily resolution) allocated per-tenant tier: premium (20% of budget reserved), standard (10%), best-effort (0-5% depending on backlog). Slices are refilled daily and can be borrowed via explicit transfer APIs.

Circuit-breaker triggers use a burn-rate window (15m and 1h) and a composite threshold: burn-rate > 3x baseline OR p99 > configured threshold OR model-quality alert delta > 2 sigma -> escalate. Actions: throttle, switch to cheaper model-variant, or fully block depending on slice and severity.

Soft-eviction strategy prioritizes thinning (reduce max concurrent requests per-route) before hard rejection. Eviction order: best-effort, background, standard, premium. Eviction is reversible and logged to budgets ledger.

Multi-region failover uses a passive warm reserve with reserved capacity equal to 10% of regional peak for critical routes. Failover requires two checks: reserve availability and degraded SLO in primary region sustained for 5m.
Error-budget accounting is token-cost-normalized: higher token routes consume more budget; budgets can be transferred with a governance API to support temporary absorption by other slices.
All enforcement decisions recorded in central ledger with correlation IDs for audit and billing reconciliation.
progress_updates: 2025-11-12: Kickoff meeting with SRE, runtime, and product. Agreed scope and SLIs to consider.

2025-11-14: Prototype SLI calculator implemented (latency + availability). Added placeholder hook for quality signal (pending Eval infra integration). Referenced Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ENDPOINT-SLI

2025-11-16: Design review with Console team — telemetry export format approved (slice_id, burn_rate_m15, burn_rate_h1, p99, quality_delta). Action: runtime to add slice_id tag to traces (ENG-31209 dependency).
2025-11-18: Initial circuit-breaker FSM drafted on Google Doc. Agreed on 15m/1h burn windows and action tiers. Filed GitHub RFC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/142

2025-11-20: Soft-eviction algorithm validated against synthetic traffic in staging (50% reduction in overall token spend with preserved premium success rate). Logged staging results dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/eviction/staging-test
notes: Model-quality signal depends on Eval infra milestones (ENG-58219). Until then, quality component will use a conservative default weight and trigger on obvious regressions only.
Billing team asked for ledger schema for cost reconciliation — added dependency for billing API contract in follow-up ticket.
Design requested a UI for slice transfer requests; scope for Console-2025.02 release.
We must avoid cascade effects: circuit-breaker actions include randomized backoff windows to prevent herd behavior during global incidents.
risks: If quality signal latency is high, circuit-breakers may not react fast enough to model regressions — mitigation: conservative fallbacks to safe model variants.
Incorrect weighting could starve best-effort customers unexpectedly — mitigation: gradual rollout with telemetry and canary quotas.
Cross-region capacity accounting edge cases could double-count reserves during simultaneous failovers — mitigation: atomic reservation checks and leader election in orchestration controller.
Operator complexity: too many knobs could increase MTTR — mitigation: sensible defaults and clear runbook steps.
